This package is R2, so the loader refuses its hardware backend until a human sets reviewed_by (R2 and R3 only).

Recon: the card's entry symbols all exist in the clone (gepace.pace:Pace gepace/pace.py:293, gepace.pace:Module gepace/pace.py:222, gepace.tango.server.pace:Pace gepace/tango/server/pace.py:41). The package drives gepace.pace:Pace, the class the README calls the core (README.md:22). DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card's helper field names PythonObjectDriver, but the package is a direct Driver (the card's decision) because the upstream interface is a Pace object with per-module Module objects (pace.modules[module], gepace/pace.py:329-340) and three extension actions, which the flat PythonObjectDriver read/write/command tables cannot express without inventing a top-level native method. The pressure-control request is the exact ':OUTP1:STAT <0|1>;:OUTP1:STAT?' setter+readback built by the upstream member (gepace/pace.py:138-184, 240) and sent through Pace.__call__ (gepace/pace.py:376-377); no command syntax was changed.

The card's candidate class cap.measure.pressure.v1 is not bound: its input requires a reference (absolute/gauge/differential), and no text file of the clone states which reference SENS1:PRES measures, so binding it would force the driver to claim a reference it cannot source. Pressure is exposed as a state read instead, in bar as the upstream tango server labels the same module value (gepace/tango/server/pace.py:118-120); the module's configured unit is exposed as pressure_unit and the raw value is not converted. The extension ids are used for the pressure-control output because no catalogue class toggles a pressure controller output (see catalogue_requests).

Limits: none. The package binds no numeric write and no numeric action input; the only action input is the boolean enabled. The pressure setpoint, source pressure, rate, rate mode and overshoot are not exposed; no text file of the clone states a setpoint range (the manuals under docs/ are PDFs, and no page was cited because no page was read), so a setpoint write was left out rather than given an invented bound. site-limits.example.json was not needed and the exemplar copy was deleted.

Safety: risk R2 because enabling the pressure control output can pressurize an external system (MHS/spec/04-safety.md R2). The @estop method and the safe-state action x-cap.tiagocoutinho.stop_pressure_control.v1 both send OUTP1:STAT 0; estop_physical_ref is not set because no text file of the clone documents an independent hardware e-stop. This is a software stop, not a safety-rated channel; the physical e-stop stays authoritative. A model-written R2 driver never runs its hardware backend until reviewed_by is set.

Fake: a deterministic in-memory stand-in for Pace and Module; every literal is placeholder test data (marked in fake.py) and none is a Fact, a Limit or a reference. The upstream sinstruments simulator was not used (it needs sinstruments and scpi, which are not installed here) and is not copied. The fake implements only upstream attributes (G7).

Warning: G8.SAFE014_NOT_APPLICABLE is expected: the package declares no limit on an actuating binding (the only input is boolean and the stop action takes no input), so SAFE-014 has nothing to probe; the in-process suite reports CL2 under that exemption, and every other CL3 test passed. Evidence remains contract_checked. There are no G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warnings.

NOT COVERED: the hardware backend (never imported or run), the pressure setpoint, source pressure, rate, rate mode, overshoot, relays, module 2, the serial and tango clients, and the upstream simulator. The pressure unit is not converted; pressure_unit reports the configured unit.
